title: Two Halves With No Repeats
statement:
You get an array nums of even length. You want to divide its elements into two groups of exactly nums.length / 2 elements each, so that neither group contains the same value twice. The groups do not have to be contiguous: any element can go into either group.

Return true if such a division exists, otherwise false.

examples.why: Groups [4, 7, 2] and [4, 7, 9]. Each repeated value sends one copy to each group.
There are three 3s and only two groups, so one group gets two of them.
There are 4 different values, more than the 3 needed per group, yet the three 1s still cannot be split. Counting distinct values is not the test.

hints: Think about one value at a time. How many copies of it can the two groups hold between them?
Each group can hold at most one copy of a value, so a value can appear at most twice in total. Is that also enough?
Count every value. The answer is true exactly when no count is larger than 2.

explain.intuition:
A value that appears three times cannot be placed: two groups, at most one copy each. So any count above 2 makes it impossible.

The other direction also holds. If every value appears at most twice, send one copy of every doubled value to each group, then fill both groups up to the half size with the single values in any way. No group ever gets a repeat, and the sizes work out because the total length is even and the doubled values split evenly.
steps: Count how many times each value appears, using a hash map.
If any count is above 2, return false.
pitfalls: Checking that there are at least n / 2 distinct values. [1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4] passes that check but is still impossible.
Treating the groups as the left and right halves of the array. Elements can go into either group.
Sorting and checking neighbours works too, but remember to look for three equal values in a row, not two.

solutions.title: Sort and look for a triple
solutions.idea: After sorting, three copies of a value sit next to each other. Check every window of three.

solutions.title: Count with a hash map
solutions.idea: No value may appear more than twice; that condition is also sufficient.

followups: Split into k equal groups with no repeats in any group. What is the condition now?
Return one valid pair of groups, not just true or false.
